# Original C11 discard-result atomic OR consumer

This self-authored header-free C function calls `__c11_atomic_fetch_or(word, 32u, __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST)` and discards the old value. Its return type is `void`. The source asserts that `unsigned int` is four bytes and contains no inline assembly. The installed clang `stdatomic.h` maps `atomic_fetch_or` to this builtin with sequentially consistent ordering; [Clang's C11 atomic builtin documentation](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/LanguageExtensions.html#c11-atomic-builtins) describes the source interface. Ring3's finite private-memory execution evidence does not establish C11 concurrent ordering.

The builder imports the unchanged scalar i686 profile and strict ordinary COFF extractor from `../p2-compiled-records/build.py`, SHA256 `fe426f202b48664a87357c766d39099b9d35b5d8217c2b114696164a0d468258`. Only the extractor's function symbol and diagnostic spelling change from `ring3_reduce` to `ring3_publish_bits`. Flags, environment, tools and COFF constraints remain fixed. A fresh output directory, tool versions, argv, source/builder/tool hashes and post-build input stability are recorded. Routine tests consume retained artifacts without invoking a compiler.

Two root-run discovery builds produced the identical whole original 9-byte text `8b442404f0830820c3`, SHA256 `95189adf43d025a695bb470bd6a0278fc4357841963731fd72129e7d00709976`. The original COFF is 529 bytes, SHA256 `3fc296b01859e54bfb5bf026912f680ee6ccf133fb4089e2306ed82289f1e312`. The original C is 180 bytes, SHA256 `607fffdec3c00b16cee151fada528e14b1e351e398fdb8a25f167f38373eada0`; the Intel disassembly is 324 bytes, SHA256 `bfd29d6deef5b616725bfa8c2218fb4a374926b45a30e474350127def3b4e731`. The only code section is `.text`; `.data` and `.bss` are empty, and `.debug$S` has 100 bytes of compiler metadata. There are no relocations or unresolved external symbols. A formal fixture build must reproduce the discovery C, object, text and disassembly before artifact publication.

The complete original function loads the pointer from `[ESP+4]`, executes `LOCK OR DWORD [EAX], 0x20` at offset 4, and naturally returns at offset 8. EAX happens to retain the pointer in this artifact; it is not a C return value. A separate 46-byte guest caller will call this unchanged original twice on one live cell, pause before the first LOCK, load memory after each natural return, and add both observations. The cell starts at `0xa5a55a5a`; the first call produces `0xa5a55a7a`, and the second performs an already-contained identity write. The caller consumes both memory values into `0x4b4ab4f4`. CPU and RAM remain live between calls, with no host reseed. The caller is distinct from the compiler-produced function.

The earlier old-return C11 `fetch_or` candidate emitted a supported LOCK CMPXCHG32 loop. Its proposed BTS dependency was falsified and retained separately in the evidence bank. This discarded-result source exposes a different original compiler path; it does not reopen that earlier hypothesis.

The product scope is exact single `F0 83 /1` memory DWORD with a signextended imm8 mask and existing 32-bit effective addresses. The [Intel OR reference](https://www.intel.com/content/dam/www/public/us/en/documents/manuals/64-ia-32-architectures-software-developer-vol-2b-manual.pdf) defines inclusive OR, sign extension, cleared CF/OF and result-derived PF/ZF/SF, with AF undefined. Ring3 reuses its ordinary logical flag policy: retain DF and reserved bit 1 (value `0x2`), compute PF/ZF/SF, and deterministically clear AF with CF/OF. The mask is a full DWORD rather than a bit index. One checked canonical helper returns the old DWORD after complete Read4 and mandatory Write4 preflight. Mask zero and already-contained identity operations remain writes, including permissions, version advancement and executable-source invalidation.

Actual evidence is planned in all four bound profiles with a valid dirty 4364-byte arena, canonical helper receipts, selected RAM/canaries, signextended masks, precise faults and repair, currentness, malformed nonforwarding packets and consumed-code identity writes. Observed counts and review results belong to the evidence bank and `result.json`; this provenance is stable before execution. The proof is finite private flat32 synchronous unshared execution. It makes no hardware locking, C11 concurrency, shared-memory ordering, full-RAM, general compatibility or performance claim. The [R3-553 task](https://linear.app/ring3-dev/issue/R3-553) records the selected contract.
